thread.title: UPDATE: This woman was fined $500 for not declaring a free apple from Delta

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: This woman was fined $500 for not declaring a free apple from Delta
text:
By Quentin Fottrell, MarketWatch
The traveler was randomly searched after a flight from Paris to Denver
Take your Apple(AAPL)iPad out of your luggage when you pass through security. And declare your apple when you go through U.S. Customs. Otherwise, you could face a hefty fine.
Crystal Tadlock was traveling from Paris to Denver last week on a Delta Air Lines(DAL) flight. During the flight, attendants passed out apples. Tadlock wasn't hungry, so she put the apple in her carry-on to eat later. That was her first mistake.
(https://twitter.com/VeganQuesoHead/status/988163867132940288)
Her second mistake was not declaring it. She was randomly searched at the airport and, because she hadn't declared the apple, was fined $500. "It's really unfortunate someone has to go through that and be treated like a criminal over a piece of fruit," Tadlock told local station Fox 31 (http://www.foxnews.com/travel/2018/04/22/woman-fined-500-for-saving-free-delta-air-lines-snack.html).
The customs agent was sarcastic and unforgiving, Tadlock said. "He had asked me if my trip to France was expensive and I said, 'Yeah.' I didn't really get why he was asking that question, and then he said, 'It's about to get a lot more expensive after I charge you $500,' " she added.
Tadlock said she now fears she will lose her Global Entry Status, a system under which preapproved, low-risk travelers can pass more quickly through airport security and customs. She is also concerned she will now be searched on future flights.
(https://twitter.com/VeganQuesoHead/status/988387491567693824)
In a statement to the Fox affiliate, Delta said it expects all customers to follow U.S. Customs and Border Protection protocols. A spokesperson for Delta told the channel that all agricultural products must be declared. (Neither organization was immediately available for comment.)
Also see:How the Trump administration is looking to change rules protecting air travelers (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-the-trump-administration-could-make-flying-even-worse-2018-03-12)
"Every fruit or vegetable must be declared to a CBP Agriculture Specialist or CBP Officer and must be presented for inspection regardless of its admissibility status," the policy states (https://help.cbp.gov/app/answers/detail/a_id/1272//food---general-food). "Fresh fruits and vegetables need to be clean and may be prohibited if they have insects or diseases."
Tadlock wrote on Twitter (https://twitter.com/VeganQuesoHead/status/988162370752004096)(TWTR) : "The problem is inconsistency with Customs. I know multiple people that were given the opportunity to throw fruit or other items away & proceed on with their lives. Also why is Delta handing out fruit that will not pass customs minutes later?"
Another flyer, Mike Labatt, said (Mine%20was%20a%20Lufthansa%20banana%20at%20LAX,%20kept%20for%20next%20leg.%20Luckily%20I%20declared%20it.%20Was%20about%20midnight,%20very%20tired.%20%e2%80%9cBut%20it%e2%80%99s%20an%20airline%20banana%e2%80%9d%20was%20genuine,%20but%20didn%e2%80%99t%20work.%20Spent%20half%20an%20hour%20x-raying%20it,%20filling%20out%20forms%20and%20educating%20me.%20So%20surprised%20that%20airlines%20keep%20doing%20this.) he had a similar issue. "Mine was a Lufthansa(LHA.XE)banana at LAX, kept for next leg. Luckily, I declared it. Was about midnight, very tired. ... Spent half an hour X-raying it, filling out forms and educating me. So surprised that airlines keep doing this."
